title: Dispatch: ambiguity-gate cube same-face reset; tighten resetsDuration and timer identity (attempt 4)
description:
Review-response dispatch for eshyra-jw56 (PR #470 got "request changes" with one
semantic blocker and two contract defects). Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` for the
original design. Branch from the CURRENT tip of `eshyra-jw56` (it now carries a
merge of origin/main).

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`, cut from
`eshyra-jw56`. Work only inside that worktree.

## P1 (blocker) — the same-face ruling canonizes an unresolved source ambiguity

SRD 5.1 says a face press makes a barrier that "lasts for 1 minute", and
separately that pressing a **different** face and expending charges resets the
duration. It never says what happens when the **already-active** face is
pressed. Both readings are defensible; there is no errata or Sage Advice
resolving it. The current PR picks "same-face resets" and hard-codes it as
canonical SRD semantics, and its own artifacts contradict each other: the PR
body and the importer test comment both say only a different face resets, while
the expectation and the generated pack mark the five same-face transitions
`resetsDuration: true`.

Per this repo's ambiguity contract, an authoritative-source ambiguity must be
recorded with multiple interpretations, `canonicalResolution: null`, and
campaign-owned runtime disposition — and the affected mechanic must cite it.
**Do not resolve the ambiguity in either direction.** Note that simply deleting
`resetsDuration` from those transitions is also wrong: it would canonize the
narrow reading silently.

### The contract already exists — for spells only

- `packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts`: `optRulesAmbiguities` (~line 934)
  validates the ambiguity block; `validateAmbiguityReferences` (~line 1046)
  rejects a declared-but-uncited ambiguity and an unknown `ambiguityId`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/validate.ts` `assertAmbiguityIdentityAndProvenance`
  (~line 274) enforces global id uniqueness and that every `source.locator`
  starts with the owning record's provenance locator. It iterates **all**
  records, so magic items get it for free once they can declare ambiguities.
- Working examples: `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/s1SummoningSpecs.ts`
  ~1653 (the ambiguity block) and ~1524 (the citation, shaped
  `{ kind: 'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:...' }`).
- **Magic-item mechanics cannot declare ambiguities today**:
  `packages/core/src/rules/magicItemMechanics.ts` ~2198 has a closed `only()`
  key list with no `ambiguities`.

### Work

1. Extract `optRulesAmbiguities` and `validateAmbiguityReferences` from
   `kindSchemas.ts` into a new shared `packages/core/src/rules/rulesAmbiguities.ts`
   and import it from both `kindSchemas.ts` and `magicItemMechanics.ts`.
   **Direction matters:** `kindSchemas.ts` imports `magicItemMechanics.ts`, so
   `magicItemMechanics.ts` must not import `kindSchemas.ts` — the shared module
   is what avoids the cycle. Spell validation behaviour must not change.
2. Generalize the citation walker to walk the whole mechanics subtree instead of
   only `effects`, so a `stateMachine.transitions[].resetsDuration` citation
   counts as a reference. For spells this is a strict superset (it can only turn
   "uncited" into "cited"); confirm the two existing spell ambiguities still
   validate.
3. Add `'ambiguities'` to the magic-item mechanics `only()` allowlist, validate
   it with the shared validator, and run the citation check over magic-item
   mechanics.
4. Widen `resetsDuration` to accept **either** `true` **or**
   `{ kind: 'source-ambiguity', ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:<kebab>' }`. Both forms
   keep the existing `from === to` rule and gain the `via` rule from P2 below.
   An ambiguity reference must resolve to an ambiguity declared on the same
   mechanics (the shared citation validator enforces this).
5. Curate the Cube of Force spec in
   `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts`:
   the five `face-N --press-face-N--> face-N` transitions carry the
   source-ambiguity form instead of `true`, and the machine's item gains:

   - `id`: `ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset`
   - `question`: whether pressing the already-active face restates the barrier's
     one-minute duration
   - `source`: two entries. Locators **must start with the record's provenance
     locator, which is `p. 215`** (e.g. `'p. 215, barrier duration'` and
     `'p. 215, different-face reset'`); `clauseId` values are plain kebab-case
     (`barrier-duration`, `different-face-reset`)
   - `affects`: five entries, one per same-face transition
   - `interpretations`: at least `same-face-resets` and
     `different-face-only-resets`, each with a `summary`
   - `canonicalResolution: null`
   - `runtimeDisposition: { status: 'engine-pending', owner: 'campaign-ruling' }`

6. Runtime (`packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`): an ambiguity-gated
   `resetsDuration` is **not** a reset — the engine keeps the conservative
   default and preserves the existing deadline, because no campaign-ruling
   facility exists yet (that is epic eshyra-jhpt). Make this non-silent: surface
   the unresolved ambiguity id(s) on `UseItemResult['transition']` (e.g.
   `unresolvedAmbiguityIds`) so a DM/campaign layer can see the gate was hit.
   Only literal `true` re-anchors.
7. Fix the contradictory comment in
   `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.test.ts`
   and update its expectation to assert the gated form. The three preserve
   rulings (cube `spell-contact-loss`, Bead of Force `move-force-sphere`, Ring
   of Shooting Stars `move-ball-lightning`) are unambiguous and stay as they are.
8. Update `docs/item-reset-executor.md`: describe the gate and state plainly
   that preserving is a provisional engine default pending campaign-ruling
   ownership, not a canonical reading of the source.

## P2 — `resetsDuration` is valid where the runtime never reads it

The validator allows the marker on any self-transition, including `timer`- and
`condition`-triggered ones, but it is only consumed while selecting an
operation-backed `via` transition; timer-fired transitions in
`itemResetExecutor.applyDueTimer` always re-anchor from the expiry deadline and
never look at it. That is a schema-valid, semantically dead declaration.

**Fix:** require `via` whenever `resetsDuration` is present (either form). Add
rejection tests for a timer-triggered and a condition-triggered declaration.

## P2 — preserved-timer identity is under-specified

`resolveItemStateTimers` matches a preserved timer with
`.find(c => c.from === from && c.to === to)`. The state-machine schema does not
forbid two timer transitions sharing a `from`/`to` pair, so in a schema-valid
machine both declarations would reuse the first preserved timer and silently
drop the second's amount, roll, and deadline.

**Fix:** enforce in `magicItemMechanics.ts` that a state machine declares at
most one `timer`-bearing transition per `from`/`to` pair, with a `RulesPackError`
naming the pair. I verified this holds across all 50 machines in the committed
pack, so it is non-breaking. Add a schema test with two same-pair timer
declarations pinning the rejection, and note in `itemTimers.ts` that the
uniqueness rule is what makes the `.find()` match unambiguous.

## Constraints

- `docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` governs the regeneration: regenerate with
  `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`,
  then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`. The generated diff should touch only
  `magic-item:cube-of-force` (five transitions change form, one ambiguities
  block appears). Anything else is a stop-and-report.
- Do NOT touch `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json`.
- Do not resolve the ambiguity, and do not add a campaign-ruling runtime — only
  the gate and the documented provisional default.
- `npm ci` first. `npm run verify:worktree` **before** committing. Commit on
  your branch. Do not push, do not open or comment on a PR, do not merge. Never
  modify eshyra-jw56.
